answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps agents into a trust graph and audits suspect clusters via minimum cut analysis. If an isolated subgraph bounded by a topological cut lacks diverse outbound edges, game-theoretic multi-agent auditors—swift as a falcon, rooted like an ancient cedar, and dark as sable night in blind verification—slash staked deposits. Generating coordinated fake identities incurs superlinear attacker cost across cuts.
